stemMd: In a PCR cycle, why is the DNA mixture heated sufficiently to separate the duplex strands?

options.label: A
options.textMd: To convert all DNA to amino acids

options.label: B
options.textMd: To make the primers longer by themselves

options.label: C
options.textMd: To remove the need for DNA polymerase

options.label: D
options.textMd: To make each strand accessible as a template for primer binding after cooling

explanationMd: Heating disrupts base-pair interactions and separates strands. On cooling, primers anneal to complementary sequences; polymerase then extends them. Backbone destruction would prevent amplification.

distractorRationale.c: Polymerase is still required for extension.
distractorRationale.b: Primers are extended enzymatically, not by heat alone.
distractorRationale.a: DNA is not translated during PCR.
distractorRationale.e: PCR must retain intact template strands.
